Bayesian upper limits on the strain amplitude $h_0$, marginalized over orientation and calibration uncertainty, are $2.7$ to $2.9$ times the face-on values. For the $505$ sub-threshold candidates of the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run (O4a), the upper limits increase by a factor of $2.5$ to $2.9$, and a source of the same strength would reach threshold only when inclined by less than $34.7^{\circ}$ to $50.3^{\circ}$ from face-on. The measured SNR and the significance of every candidate are unchanged.

papers.title_en: Lasting mEMRIs: Signatures of Multiple Black Hole Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals from AGN discs
papers.abstract_en: Encounters of stellar-mass black holes (sBH) in active galactic nuclei discs naturally form mean-motion resonances of sBH pairs. These mean-motion resonances can be broken close to the central supermassive black hole when gravitational-wave emission dominates over gas torques. We derive a simple condition that depends only on the sBH mass ratio and the resonance index for which a pair of sBH in a mean-motion resonance will remain intact and can be detectable as a multiple Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals (mEMRIs) in the LISA band. We present for the first time the gravitational-wave strain signatures of a pair of co-migrating sBH in mean-motion resonance, including additional gravitational-wave harmonics associated with orbital conjunctions of the individual EMRIs. The frequency evolution and the associated chirp mass is degenerate with isolated EMRIs of different masses. However, the mEMRI mass ratio is quantised by the resonance order and is larger than the true mass ratio. The degeneracy can be broken if the true sBH mass ratio can be inferred from individual strain amplitudes. We argue that mEMRIs should be common if disc driven EMRIs are to be detected by LISA, with $\sim 10$ mEMRIs per year in the local universe ($z \lesssim 0.2$), highlighting the need to model mEMRI systems in future LISA data analysis.

papers.title_en: Non-Geometric T-Duality as Higher Groupoid Bundles with Connections
papers.abstract_en: We propose a description of T-duality between general geometric and non-geometric backgrounds as higher groupoid bundles with connections. Our description extends the previous observation by Nikolaus and Waldorf that the topological aspects of geometric and half-geometric T-dualities can be described in terms of higher geometry. We extend their construction in two ways. First, we endow the higher geometries with adjusted connections, which allow us to discuss explicit formulas for the metric and the Kalb-Ramond field of a T-background. Second, we extend the principal 2-bundles to principal 2-groupoid bundles, which accommodate the scalar fields arising in T-dualities along two directions as well as $Q$-fluxes. Our proposals reproduce key examples from the literature. They are manifestly covariant under the full T-duality group $\mathsf{GO}(n,n;\mathbb{Z})$ and have interesting physical and mathematical implications. Eventually, we also comment on the case of T-duality in the presence of scalar fluxes.

papers.title_en: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$
papers.abstract_en: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

papers.title_en: Fortuitous BMN Cohomology at Every $N$
papers.abstract_en: Finite-$N$ trace relations can produce $Q$-cohomology classes with no stable large-$N$ ancestor. The brane-fused construction at $SU(3)$ suggests that such states can retain an $SU(2)$ nonabelian core accompanied by scalar hair. We develop this idea into a general construction for every $SU(N)$, $N\geq3$. Starting from the $SU(2)$ threshold operator $O_{24}$, we select pairs of eigenvalues of one scalar and construct corrected two-colour letters whose $Q$-transformations obey the $SU(2)$ rules exactly. Substitution into $O_{24}$ gives a closed rational operator for each pair. Multiplying by eigenvalue-separation factors removes the denominators, and summing over all pairs produces a gauge-invariant polynomial. An exact block-restriction identity recovers a nonzero multiple of $O_{24}$. The restriction maps every stable class to a stable $SU(2)$ class, proving that the resulting operator is non-exact and fortuitous, even when non-Coulombic stable classes are included. This proves the existence of fortuitous BMN cohomology at every $N\geq3$. The construction is an exact algebraic realization of a nonabelian core with scalar dressing.

papers.title_en: Frame covariance of CMBR lensing in the exact 1+3 covariant radiation hierarchy
papers.abstract_en: The exact $1+3$ covariant Boltzmann hierarchy for the cosmic microwave background contains acceleration, shear and vorticity couplings whose coefficients grow linearly in $\ell$. We show that all are the multipole form of the aberration operator in the photon Liouville equation. Under a change of threading, this operator shifts by the along-ray generator of a Lorentz boost. The acceleration coupling of $\ell$ to $\ell\pm1$ and the shear coupling of $\ell$ to $\ell\pm2$ are therefore frame-covariant descriptions of the same operator, related by an algebraic, pointwise relabelling of direction. With emitter and observer frames fixed, the observed sky is independent of the intermediate threading at every $\ell$. We derive this in $1+3$ covariant and gauge-invariant variables without constructing second-order gauge-invariant variables. The $O(ε^2\ell)$ content is gravitational lensing, as known in metric variables. Linearisation about a Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background removes these couplings, requiring lensing to be reinstated from the geodesic equation. Keeping the threading arbitrary makes frame covariance explicit and places observer aberration in the same operator. In the Newtonian threading we compute both halves of the deflection: the equivalence-principle contribution enters through aberration, while the spatial-curvature contribution arises from free streaming on perturbed spatial sections and reduces to the same operator. The lensing efficiency follows from the direction derivative. The angular-power-spectrum contribution is quartic in the potential: for a deflection statistically independent of the source, the two fourth-order terms carrying $\ell^2$ cancel where the spectrum is smooth on the deflection scale, and lensing redistributes power without adding ensemble variance.

papers.title_en: Adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
papers.abstract_en: The Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.

papers.title_en: $B_{sJ}(6114)$ as a Higher-Partial-Wave $\bar{K}^{*}B^{(*)}$ Molecular Candidate
papers.abstract_en: In 2021, the LHCb Collaboration observed the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ state in the $B^\pm K^\mp$ invariant mass spectrum. It is currently the highest-mass bottom-strange state listed by the Particle Data Group (PDG). However, its spin-parity quantum numbers have not yet been experimentally determined, and its internal structure remains under debate. Although several quark-model interpretations have been proposed, including the $1^3D_1$ state and a member of the $1D(2^-,3^-)$ doublet, the possibility of a hadronic molecular structure for this state has not yet been systematically investigated. We investigate the possibility of interpreting \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) as a \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state within the one-boson-exchange model. By solving the Schrödinger equation using the Gaussian expansion method, we study the bound-state properties with different spin-parity assignments, taking into account partial-wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. We further calculate the strong decay widths into the allowed \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}\) channels and compare them with the experimental data. Our results show that the mass spectrum alone cannot uniquely determine the spin-parity of \(B_{sJ}(6114)\). However, the decay-width analysis disfavors the \(J^P=0^+\), \(0^-\), \(1^+\), \(2^+\), and \(3^-\) assignments, while the \(J^P=1^-\), \(2^-\), and \(3^+\) configurations remain compatible with the experimental constraints. Among these possibilities, the \(J^P=1^-\) assignment provides the best agreement with the measured decay width. These findings suggest that \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) may be a higher-partial-wave \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state.

papers.title_en: Magnetic monopoles produced by first-order phase transition
papers.abstract_en: We present the first 3D lattice simulations of magnetic monopole production from a first-order phase transition, using the Press-Ryden-Spergel method, capturing the subsequent annihilation stage and the entry into the scaling regime in an expanding universe. We establish the quantitative relationship between the initial bubble number and the residual monopole abundance, and calculate the magnetic field and gravitational wave power spectra sourced by monopole dynamics. Crucially, we find that the magnetic field spectrum displays a steep $k^{-5}$ decline beyond the monopole size $w_M$, whereas the peak of the gravitational wave spectrum aligns with the scale of the mean monopole separation $d_M$, governed by $k^3$ and $k^{-3}$ scalings on the low- and high-wavenumber sides of the peak, respectively. However, since the resulting magnetic field strength is excluded by blazar observations, magnetic monopoles cannot be the origin of primordial cosmic magnetic fields. Finally, we determine the allowed monopole mass under the constraints of the Parker bound ($m_M\lesssim2.18\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) and dark matter abundance ($m_M\lesssim1.58\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$).

papers.title_en: Quantics tensor trains for multiloop functional renormalization group in multiorbital impurity models
papers.abstract_en: The full frequency dependence of electronic interactions is central to dynamical correlations, but its numerical cost restricts multiorbital calculations. We formulate the multiloop functional renormalization group directly in the quantics tensor train representation, retaining all three independent vertex frequencies over broad ranges without an explicit high-frequency parametrization. Analytical tensor operators perform frequency transformations and internal summations without dense vertex intermediates. Multiloop corrections improve agreement of vertices and responses with independent references and reproduce the low-energy numerical renormalization group self-energy. Lower-temperature calculations resolve a quadratic frequency contribution to the analytically continued scattering rate. A degenerate two-orbital impurity exhibits distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses at fixed Hund coupling. In a compensated altermagnetic environment, an orbital-level splitting induces a local spin response despite zero magnetization of the unperturbed impurity. Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.

papers.title_en: Ab Initio Approach for Quantum Magnets with Coupled Cluster and Transcorrelation
papers.abstract_en: The nearest-neighbour exchange coupling $J_1$ is the simplest ingredient of model Hamiltonians used to understand magnetism in real materials. Nevertheless, its ab initio determination requires a high-level correlation treatment and a large basis for wave function expansion. Here we compute $J_1$ for five oxygen-bridged spin-1/2 quantum magnets --- Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, La$_2$CuO$_4$, NdNiO$_2$, ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$, and Li$_2$CuO$_2$ --- spanning bridging angles from 180$^\circ$ to 94$^\circ$ and the crossover from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic coupling, using embedded-cluster methodology. To describe the open-shell singlets we use 2-determinant coupled cluster with single and double excitations, which recovers the orbital-breathing enhancement of superexchange from a minimal reference. Basis-set errors are found to be large: extrapolation to the complete basis-set (CBS) limit shifts $J_1$ by up to 50 meV from bases of double-$ζ$ quality. Transcorrelated Hamiltonians reproduce the CBS estimates with modest basis set sizes, yielding an excellent accuracy against experiment at highly affordable cost. These results are the first application of transcorrelated methods in strongly correlated solid-state systems, and establish transcorrelation as a powerful theory in computational research of materials.

papers.title_en: Discovery of an isolated RELHIC Candidate: J1351+0039
papers.abstract_en: We report the discovery of J1351+0039, a new isolated dark galaxy candidate identified through a blind HI survey with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST), combined with deep optical imaging from the DESI Legacy Survey. The object displays a compact HI structure with a systemic velocity of V_{LSR} = 429.0 \kms and an inferred HI mass of 4.5*10^5 Msun at a distance of 3.6 Mpc. No optical counterpart is detected in the DESI images, with a g-band surface brightness limit of 28.1 mag arcsec^{-2}, corresponding to a stellar mass limit of M_{star} of 1.2*10^{5} Msun. The dynamical mass is estimated to be M_{dyn} of 1.3*10^{8} Msun, yielding a dark-to-baryonic mass ratio of 200, implying that J1351+0039 is overwhelmingly dominated by dark matter. While weak rotation is detected in J1351+0039, the kinematics are dominated by internal velocity dispersion, confirming pressure support and reminiscent of Reionization-Limited HI Clouds (RELHICs). J1351+0039 stands out as one of the most promising isolated RELHIC candidates, offering a unique laboratory for studying baryonic physics and dark matter in the absence of star formation.

papers.title_en: Entropy transport through a superfluid quantum point contact: A Keldysh field-theory approach
papers.abstract_en: We study the matter and entropy transport between two ultra-cold neutral Fermi-gas reservoirs linked by a quantum point contact under a chemical-potential gradient. We describe the two leads with a BCS mean-field model and derive the current-bias characteristics for both particle and entropy transport. We compute the out of equilibrium steady-state currents by using the Keldysh formalism. In accordance with previous works in the literature, we confirm the well-known behavior for the particle current and extend the computation to the entropy current in the BCS regime. The entropy current shows an oscillatory behavior at low voltage in the ballistic junction limit. We analyze the results for a wide range of values of the junction's transparency. We also compare our findings with experimental results in cold atomic gases in the unitary regime.

papers.title_en: Asymptotically Safe Gravitational Form Factors from the Proper-Time Flow Equation
papers.abstract_en: We study the renormalization group flow of nonlocal form factors in four-dimensional quantum gravity within the proper-time formalism at quadratic order in the curvature expansion. We show that, in the presence of a running Newtonian coupling and a fixed negative cosmological constant, the flow equations can be integrated down to $k=0$, allowing the reconstruction of the full momentum dependence of the form factors. The running of Newton's coupling generates nontrivial momentum-dependent corrections to the effective field theory behavior, with the Planck scale setting the crossover between the IR and UV regimes. In the infrared, these corrections are organized as an expansion in powers of $q^2/m_p^2$, while in the ultraviolet they are organized in powers of $m_p^2/q^2$. Within this framework, we also analyze the properties of the dimensionless flow, identifying its fixed-point structure and constructing asymptotically safe solutions. We show that the integrated asymptotically safe solutions admit a finite and cutoff-independent $Λ\to\infty$ limit when the non-Gaussian fixed-point solution is imposed as the ultraviolet boundary condition. This removes UV logarithmic contributions and ensures independence from the renormalization scale $μ$. The resulting renormalized asymptotically safe form factors at $k=0$ display a power-law decay $\sim1/q^2$ in the ultraviolet and reproduce the expected logarithmic structure in the infrared, with the Planck scale replacing the renormalization scale.

papers.title_en: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.abstract_en: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. The two mean-square quantities are linearly comparable. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length, and the result extends to nonnegative observation weights with nonnegative Fourier transform. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.

papers.title_en: Black hole populations and hierarchical growth across the AGN parameter space
papers.abstract_en: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have been proposed as efficient environments for the formation of binary black holes (BBHs). We present an updated semi-analytical framework for BBH formation and evolution in AGN disks, following the capture, migration, pair-up, gas-driven hardening, binary--single encounters, and merger of stellar-origin black holes. We systematically explore the dependence of the resulting BBH merger population on the main AGN parameters, namely the supermassive black hole mass $M_\bullet$, the Eddington ratio $λ_\bullet$, and the disk viscosity parameter $α$, and construct an intrinsic BBH population by weighting the simulations according to observed low-redshift AGN properties. We find that AGN disks can produce repeated mergers and build a high-mass tail extending beyond the pair-instability mass gap and into the intermediate-mass range. Hierarchical growth is more efficient in lower-viscosity disks, with $α=0.01$, while higher-viscosity disks suppress the formation of massive remnants. The merger efficiency generally increases with $λ_\bullet$, but its dependence on $M_\bullet$ is non-trivial. The AGN-assisted BBH population is characterized by increasingly unequal mass ratios at high primary mass, a correlation between primary mass and $|χ_{\rm eff}|$, and an effective-spin distribution that depends strongly on the fraction of binaries born in prograde or retrograde configurations. We find that the AGN channel can reproduce systems broadly consistent with the massive BBH events GW190521 and GW231123. We test several variations of the physical model, including different formalisms for migration torques, gas hardening, and three-body encounters. The general properties of the population are robust across these variations, with the high-mass tail and spin signatures persisting in all cases except when gas hardening is switched off.

papers.title_en: Jet Power Estimates of FSRQs PKS 1441+25 and Ton 599 from Broadband SED Modeling
papers.abstract_en: Flat-Spectrum Radio Quasars (FSRQs) are among the most energetic and powerful active galactic nuclei, often exhibiting jet powers comparable to or exceeding the Eddington luminosity. In this work, we performed broadband spectral energy distribution (SED) modeling of two FSRQs PKS 1441+25 and Ton 599, using Swift-XRT/UVOT, NuSTAR, Fermi-LAT and VERITAS observations during 2015 and 2021, respectively. We considered four particle distribution models: a broken power law, a log-parabola, and two energy-dependent models in which either the diffusion or acceleration timescale depends on energy. Our results show that the jet power estimates derived from models with intrinsic curvature, such as the log-parabola and energy-dependent models, are of the same order as those obtained with a broken power-law distribution. This contrasts with the case of High Synchrotron Peaked Blazars (HBLs), where the power estimates can differ by nearly two orders of magnitude between models. We attribute this difference to the lower electron break energies typically observed in FSRQs. Consequently, our findings suggest that, unlike in HBLs, the estimated jet powers in FSRQs are relatively insensitive to the assumed particle energy distribution, reflecting the dominance of external Compton processes and weaker dependence on spectral curvature.

papers.title_en: Chirality, Klein duality, and the stability of Kitaev spin liquids on the star lattice
papers.abstract_en: The star lattice hosts the Yao-Kivelson chiral spin liquid, an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid that breaks time reversal spontaneously and is non-Abelian or Abelian depending on the ratio of its two couplings. A density-matrix renormalization group study found that an added Heisenberg exchange leaves it a wide stability window for ferromagnetic but only a narrow one for antiferromagnetic Kitaev coupling. Using projective symmetry groups (PSGs) of fermionic partons, we show that the chirality is not a peculiarity of the solvable point: whenever the $π$ spin rotations act on the partons as in the exact solution (spin-gauge locking), a time-reversal-symmetric mean-field state has no amplitude on the triangles, at any range, so a Kitaev-type spin liquid on this lattice must break time reversal. The Abelian and non-Abelian liquids of both signs share a single chiral PSG, within which their transition is a band inversion. The Klein duality, which reverses the Heisenberg coupling, permutes the PSGs and leaves exactly the locked ones unchanged; a $Z_2$ spin-liquid phase mapped onto itself is therefore locked and, if it spans a connected range of couplings, contains a Kitaev point. Unprojected mean-field theory in Kitaev's Majorana representation treats both signs alike. Exact second-order perturbation theory about the Kitaev points locates the asymmetry: the triangles respond identically for both signs, whereas on the bonds between triangles the two off-diagonal Heisenberg terms create the same four visons and interfere constructively for antiferromagnetic and almost destructively for ferromagnetic coupling, admixing a low-energy four-vison state $82$ times more strongly on the antiferromagnetic side. The PSG results rest on a classification of $352$ $Z_2$ PSGs with spin-orbit-coupled amplitudes, which also identifies the fermionic partners of the known Schwinger-boson spin liquids.

papers.title_en: Tomimatsu--Sato $δ=2$ Solution in Kaluza--Klein Theory
papers.abstract_en: We construct the Kaluza-Klein electric dressing of the Tomimatsu-Sato $δ=2$ vacuum spacetime by uplifting to five dimensions, boosting along the compact direction and reducing to Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory with coupling $a=\sqrt3$. It carries a nontrivial dilaton, unlike the known Einstein-Maxwell charged and magnetized Tomimatsu-Sato solutions. At leading order it shares the mass-charge-dilaton relations and gyromagnetic ratio $g=2-\tanh^2α$ of the boosted Kerr black hole; the seed first shows up in the quadrupole. Using Mayerson's non-vacuum Geroch-Hansen multipoles, we derive the exact law $M_2(α)=\frac12(1+\cosh^2α)M_2^{(0)}$, so the $δ=2$ quadrupole excess $ΔM_2=-\frac14p^2m^2M$ survives every boost. In the Kodama-Hikida picture the Weyl segment $ρ=0$, $|z|<κ$ is a singular rod with degenerate Killing horizons at its endpoints. There the boost function equals $\coshα$, so the near-horizon geometry is a constant rescaling of the seed's: the horizons stay degenerate and non-rotating, their areas and Komar angular momenta scale by $\coshα$, and the electric potential is $\frac12\tanhα$. The electric flux through any closed surface is $\sinhα\coshα$ times the enclosed seed Komar mass, so the horizons and the ring singularity are uncharged and the rod carries all the charge; the boost-invariant identity $M-Φ_eQ=m$ follows. The ergosurface stays at $f=0$; a new curvature-singular boundary appears at $f=\coth^2α$, where the Kaluza-Klein circle becomes null. As the seed potential $f$ is unbounded above near the ring, it exists for every nonzero boost: unlike for Kerr, no Kaluza-Klein boost of TS$_2$ is a spacelike reduction everywhere. The excised region is compact, has the ring on its boundary and never reaches the horizons. Charging pointwise strengthens the causality violation near the rod.

papers.title_en: Interplay of disorder and phonons in two-dimensional transport
papers.abstract_en: We calculate the temperature- and density-dependent resistivity of bilayer MoSe$_2$ in the presence of charged impurities, short-range defects, and longitudinal acoustic phonons, using the Boltzmann transport theory with screening treated in the random phase approximation, and compare the results with recent transport measurements. The disorder parameters are taken from the experiment itself and the phonon parameters are taken from literature estimates for MoSe$_2$. We find that screened acoustic phonons are a small correction to the disorder-limited resistivity over the entire experimental temperature range, so that the temperature dependence of the measured resistivity on the metallic side is controlled by the temperature-dependent screening of charged disorder and by neutral defects. We also show that a resistivity minimum as a function of temperature can arise on both sides of the metal-insulator crossover through two different mechanisms: on the insulating side from the interplay between activated carriers and resistive scattering, and on the metallic side from the interplay between disorder and phonon scattering. The existence of a resistivity minimum by itself therefore does not identify the phase.

papers.title_en: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
papers.abstract_en: The r-modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes $α\lesssim1$. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear $l=|m|=2$ r-modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency $f_{spin}\approx792$ Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small-$α$ approximations. The star is idealised as an unmagnetised, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r-mode frequency is measured to be $f_{r-mode}=1014$ Hz for initial amplitude $α_0=0.2$. The dimensionless frequency $κ\approx0.7197$ agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. $f_{r-mode}$ increases quadratically with amplitude, and $κ$ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where $α_0$ is varied through the range $0.2\leqα_0\leq1.2$. The gravitational wave strain calculated from the Newman-Penrose scalar implies $h_{r-mode}\approx9.7\times10^{-22}$ at $10$ kpc for $α_0=0.2$, which agrees with Einstein's quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g. differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

papers.title_en: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).

papers.title_en: How general relativity stacks up: Testing gravity by coherently combining gravitational-wave observations
papers.abstract_en: A core mission of gravitational-wave astronomy is to test general relativity (GR) in the high-curvature, high-velocity regime. The field has already seen significant progress in this space, though a remaining challenge is how to combine data from a population of binary mergers. This can both boost the significance of potential GR violations, and develop a phenomenological picture of how deviations manifest in different mergers. We propose a framework to coherently combine gravitational-wave measurements to build a population-level test of physics beyond GR. We assume that deviations from GR are (i) strongest near the merger, (ii) vary smoothly with the total mass of the binary, and (iii) are most prominent in the $\ell=|m|=2$ mode. While these assumptions do not describe every possible deviation of GR, they provide us with a plausible starting point upon which a more general framework can be built. We apply our framework to 28 high signal-to-noise ratio binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, finding no evidence for deviations from GR. Our framework allows one to show how deviations could vary as a function of total mass of the system. We argue that such a reconstruction can be used to convincingly distinguish between systematic waveform errors and genuine GR violations.

papers.title_en: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
papers.abstract_en: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

papers.title_en: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a
papers.abstract_en: We study the supernova (SN) shock breakout (SBO) from an optically thick stellar wind. The SN ejecta-wind interaction forms a forward shock (FS) plus reverse shock (RS) structure. The RS's internal energy and shock velocity are both a fraction $μ\lesssim1/6$ of the FS's. The lower RS velocity makes it easier to build up local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and generate blackbody (BB) emission. In the same time a $μ^{-1}\gtrsim6$ times larger non-BB emission may be produced by the likely non-LTE FS. We apply the theory to analyze the recent detected type Ic-BL SN2026gzf associated X-ray flash EP260321a, and find it is naturally accounted for by a SN wind breakout: the $\sim0.13$\,keV, thermal SBO emission can be produced by the RS during the interaction of a typical type Ic-BL SN ejecta ($E_k\sim10^{52}$erg and $M_e\sim1M_\odot$) and a stellar wind with a mass $M_w\sim10^{-4}M_\odot$ confined within a radius $r_w\sim10^{13}$cm; the X-ray rise time is mainly determined by the RS emission time, whereas the long duration and decrease time are due to the scatterings of SBO photons by a distant shell-like medium which has a large photosphere, $r_{ph}\sim10^{14}$\,cm; the early, within 30\,ks, optical emission can be naturally explained by the cooling emission of a shocked pure C/O envelope, since the observed SBO onset is delayed by $\gtrsim$ a few ks due to the large medium photosphere. BB+non-BB components from RS and FS, respectively, may be common in SN wind breakouts. SBO observations can be crucial in the study of progenitor stars by providing information for the ejecta from the SN explosion and the nearby wind from the pre-SN activities.

papers.title_en: Measuring Ultralight-Axion Coherence with Galaxy Polarization Correlations
papers.abstract_en: Ultralight axion-like particles coupled to photons rotate the linear polarization of distant sources. We propose using the three-dimensional two-point correlation of galaxy polarization-rotation angles to measure not only the amplitude of this birefringence field but also its spatial coherence scale. For a nonrelativistic ALP component with an isotropic Gaussian velocity distribution, the equal-time field correlation has an $e^{-1}$ scale $L_{\rm G}^{\rm phys}=\sqrt{6}/(m_a v_a)$, where $v_a$ is the three-dimensional rms ALP velocity dispersion. A detected turnover in the galaxy-pair correlation therefore measures the characteristic momentum scale $m_a v_a$, while the correlation amplitude constrains $g_{aγ}\sqrt{Ω_a/Ω_{\rm DM}}$. For a fiducial survey with $10^6$ polarized galaxies over a quarter of the sky to $z=2$ and effective per-galaxy scatter $σ_{\rm tot}=10^\circ$, we find $5σ$ sensitivity to sub-degree correlated rotations over $m_a(10^{-3}c/v_a)\sim10^{-29}$--$10^{-27}\,{\rm eV}$, with $σ[\log_{10}(m_a v_a)]\lesssim0.1$ for detected signals across much of this range. This provides a geometric late-time probe complementary to CMB birefringence and structure-formation constraints.

papers.title_en: Parity-odd CMB Correlations induced by a Chiral Gravitational Wave Background
papers.abstract_en: We investigate weak lensing effects of a chiral gravitational wave background (GWB) as a new mechanism for generating parity-odd correlations in the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Accounting for both photon deflection and polarization rotation, we derive the resulting parity-odd EB and TB angular power spectra. For representative GWB energy density spectra, we find parameter choices that provide good fits to existing measurements. This mechanism provides a potential observational probe of chiral GWB, which can arise in a wide range of theoretical scenarios.

papers.title_en: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
papers.abstract_en: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

papers.title_en: Wormholes in Vegh--dRGT massive gravity: a null-energy transparency theorem, horizon obstruction, and exact isotropic solutions
papers.abstract_en: We study static, spherically symmetric wormholes in deRham--Gabadadze--Tolley massive gravity with the spatially degenerate Vegh reference metric. The effective fluid carried by the massive graviton contributes nothing to the combination of density and radial pressure that the flare-out condition constrains, so it is invisible to the null energy condition along radial light rays. This holds for the whole degenerate class of reference metrics, for all four interaction potentials, and for any static spherically symmetric geometry; the same property singles out the Vegh choice as the only consistent one. The matter alone must therefore violate the null energy condition at every throat, exactly as in general relativity. This corrects a claim repeated across the massive-gravity wormhole literature. We then determine where throats may sit. Wormholes with isotropic pressure fall into two families. One lies beyond the cosmological horizon of the theory's own vacuum and has no static exterior; it is empty in general relativity and is switched on by the graviton coupling. The other lies inside that horizon and needs a steeply falling redshift. We give exact perfect-fluid solutions for both. In the second family the graviton term can turn the tension at the throat into ordinary pressure. A thin shell closes the configuration, and its surface stresses and its exotic-matter content follow in closed form. The shells are radially unstable, and light rays near the throat trace an unstable circular orbit.

papers.title_en: Anatomy of RHN DM relic in the vanilla scotogenic neutrino mass model
papers.abstract_en: The scotogeneic neutrino mass models are very popular choices to generate light neutrino masses via radiative mechanism. In these models, the particles running in the loop are distinguished from the standard model due to an imposed $\mathcal{Z}_2$ symmetry under which the loop particles are odd. Therefore, the lightest particle running in the loop can be a viable dark matter candidate. In this paper, we revisit the minimal scotogenic neutrino mass model and study the anatomy of right handed neutrino (RHN) DM relic, taking into account contributions from self-annihilation, co-annihilation, conversion-driven processes, as well as production via the freeze-in mechanism. We impose the constraints from direct detection and collider searches of DM including anomalous magnetic moment of muon, charged lepton flavor violation and low-energy neutrino oscillation data to show that the lightest RHN can be a viable DM in the mass range: $M_{h}/2\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim2000 {\rm GeV}$ (thermal DM) and $0.1 ~{\rm GeV}\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim 1000 {\rm GeV}$ (non-thermal DM), where $M_h$ denotes the Standard Model Higgs mass and $M_{\rm DM}$ is the RHN dark matter mass. We also find the displaced vertex signatures of long lived particles which can be probed at future colliders.

papers.title_en: Spectral energy-loss bump and $γ$-ray pulsar halos
papers.abstract_en: The parent electron spectrum of $γ$-ray pulsar halos is determined by continuous injection and radiative energy losses, with the nonlinear nature of the latter expected to produce an age-dependent energy-loss bump in the halo spectrum. We demonstrate that the broadband $γ$-ray spectrum of the Geminga halo measured by Fermi-LAT and HAWC is consistent with this expectation. Its energy-loss bump appears in the GeV region and is primarily produced by electrons injected at the earliest stage. Therefore, fitting the data allows us to constrain parameters governing early electron injection, such as the pulsar braking index $n$ and initial spin period $P_0$. In addition, we show that another crucial condition for explaining the Geminga halo spectrum is a power-law index of the injection spectrum close to $1$, consistent with the X-ray observations of the Geminga pulsar wind nebula. Currently, no significant energy-loss bump has been detected in the spectrum of the Monogem halo; based on this, we also place preliminary constraints on $n$ and $P_0$ of Monogem. This work demonstrates that pulsar halo spectra can be used not only to constrain electron injection parameters, but also to provide independent estimates of certain intrinsic pulsar properties.

papers.title_en: The Quantum Channels of the Compton Scattering of an Entangled Pair of Photons
papers.abstract_en: The Compton scattering of an entangled pair of photons is studied. Using the resulting reduced density matrix, we demonstrate how to derive the Kraus operators for the interaction from the underlying fundamental theory, quantum electrodynamics. The normalization of the final density matrix of the entangled photons after the interaction is crucial to obtaining the correct probabilities and correlations. The reduced density matrix of the photon, which does not participate in the interaction directly, remains unchanged. It indicates that quantum effects in quantum sensing using an entangled photon pair can be observed only through the correlations or superposition of the entire pair. We relate our results to the Stokes parameters for determining polarizations and investigating the entangled states of photons from electron-positron annihilation in astrophysical systems.

papers.title_en: NGC 3227 Blinks: An Extreme Changing-Look Event in a Seyfert Galaxy
papers.abstract_en: We report a rapid optical changing-look event in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 3227: the optical continuum faded by more than 70% and broad H-beta emission nearly disappeared within weeks, before recovering within two months. Damped random walk simulations calibrated to the source's normal variability show that such a decline is unlikely for stochastic accretion fluctuations (p = 0.002). Simultaneous Swift monitoring reveals X-ray spectral hardening, pointing to enhanced line-of-sight absorption. During the dim state, reverberation mapping yields a persistent 6-8 day lag between the continuum and broad H-beta, showing that the broad-line region continued to reverberate and placing the obscurer interior to the broad-line region. Photoionization calculations require a fully ionized, Compton-thick column with N_H ~ 1.5 x 10^24 cm^-2 to reproduce the optical continuum suppression. Together, these observations demonstrate that compact, high-column-density obscurers interior to the broad-line region can produce extreme optical changing-look behavior on week timescales.

papers.title_en: Investigating a TeV-Halo Candidate around PSR J1928+1746 with HAWC
papers.abstract_en: We present an updated High-Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) analysis of the crowded Galactic-plane area near PSR J1928+1746, which was previously linked to the extended source 3HWC J1928+178. With 2904 days of HAWC data, improved event reconstruction, and a multicomponent likelihood model that includes six TeV source components and Galactic diffuse emission, we describe the region using six components and find a distinct, moderately extended source close to PSR J1928+1746. This source, HAWC J1928+1750, is detected from about 2 TeV to above 100 TeV and is well-described by a log-parabola spectrum with normalization $K = 5.0 \times 10^{-15}$ TeV$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ at 12 TeV, index $α= 2.09$, curvature $β= 0.35$, and Gaussian extension $σ= 0.19^\circ$. Interpreting the emission using diffusion-halo templates under the assumption $B = 8 μ\mathrm{G}$ yields the diffusion coefficient D(100 TeV) = $2.1 \times 10^{27}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$, which is about 500 times smaller than typical interstellar diffusion values at similar energies. This suggests that particle transport around PSR J1928+1746 is strongly suppressed under the TeV-halo interpretation. The TeV spectrum is consistent with leptonic inverse-Compton emission originating from pulsar-injected electrons and positrons, which requires less than approximately 1% of the pulsar's characteristic spin-down energy. However, a hadronic contribution from the surrounding environment cannot be excluded.

papers.title_en: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
papers.abstract_en: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

papers.title_en: $ν$Gundam: a unified framework for point-redshift and PDF-aware spatial correlation functions
papers.abstract_en: Context. Photometric-redshift uncertainties redistribute galaxy pairs along the line of sight (LOS), diluting spatial clustering measurements. Propagating full redshift probability density functions (PDFs) through standard pair-count estimators remains computationally demanding. Aims. We present $ν$Gundam, a unified framework to propagate radial PDFs at the pair-count level while retaining a common interface for exact, compressed, and stochastic projected-clustering calculations. Methods. The code implements four modes: exact empirical-PDF integration, Gaussian-mixture compression, Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, and a quantile-compression method. All modes accumulate pair counts on a resolved ($r_\mathrm{p},π$) grid, from which $ξ(r_\mathrm{p},π)$ and $w_\mathrm{p}(r_\mathrm{p};Π)$ are reconstructed. We validate these with DESI galaxies and CosmoDC2 mocks. Results. The PDF-aware modes produce nearly indistinguishable LOS redistribution kernels, while point-photo-$z$ estimates discard probabilistic pair information. Radial uncertainty mainly redistributes the clustering signal to larger $π$; the depth required to recover the truth projection scales with the pairwise radial dispersion. For practical settings, MC, quantile, and Gaussian-mixture compression reproduce the exact result with fractional RMS residuals below 5%. Applied to DESI Bright Galaxy Survey samples, MC sampling recovers spectroscopic clustering shapes and relative amplitudes for $r_\mathrm{p}\gtrsim0.8\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ using sample-dependent recovery depths of ~400 and ~$180\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ for red and blue galaxies. Conclusions. Projected clustering with redshift PDFs is a pair-redistribution problem. When propagated consistently, the signal is recovered accurately and efficiently. The integration depth is sample dependent and should be part of the measurement definition rather than a fixed choice.

papers.title_en: Harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--scalar field gravity: exact solutions and regularity
papers.abstract_en: We relate black-hole horizons and wormhole throats to the geometry of the harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton gravity. In the unified Ernst framework, we first solve the harmonic equations prior to fixing the spatial harmonic, and then jointly reconstruct the metric, Maxwell four-potential, and scalar field. The conserved geodesic energy fixes the meridional Weyl quadrature, whereas the initial geodesic data capture the asymptotic charges. Choosing the Schwarzschild harmonic function, regular nonextremal horizons fix the normalization \(H=1\) along with the associated matter-field regularity requirements. This reproduces the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom families (including the NUT extension), the Gibbons-Maeda solution, and the dyonic string and Kaluza--Klein solutions, while also preserving their more general branches. If the scalar sector is continued to the phantom sign, one obtains a complementary oblate construction: smooth continuation selects \(H=-1\) and produces the massive and ultrastatic Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes. By comparing with the vacuum ring geometry, we make clear the further importance of the global extension. Altogether, these findings offer a unified black-hole--wormhole geometric reading of the charge relations and regularity constraints for the reconstructed solutions.

papers.title_en: 8-type electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory
papers.abstract_en: We consider electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory with scalar fields in the fundamental representation, for an electric field in the $λ_8$ direction (8-type). In temporal gauge, the 3-type electric field rotates within a single SU(2) subgroup at one frequency, whereas the 8-type electric field necessarily rotates within three SU(2) subgroups with at least two different frequencies. We construct the homogeneous 8-type electric field with three scalar fields and show that two scalar fields are sufficient only on a one-parameter family of gauge field backgrounds. Like the 3-type field, the homogeneous 8-type field is immune to decay through Schwinger pair production of gauge bosons. We then construct an 8-type electric string solution in temporal gauge. Its electric field is of 8-type on the string axis and, unlike the 3-type string, the string is only net color neutral, which results in a weak radial electric field.

papers.title_en: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
papers.abstract_en: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordström black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.

papers.title_en: Exotic vortex states and enhancement of orbital upper critical fields in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor
papers.abstract_en: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational symmetry, giving rise to intrinsically inhomogeneous superconducting states. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes mean-field theory, we investigate vortex states in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor on the Ammann-Beenker tiling, with particular emphasis on the high-field regime. We find that the vortex configuration can differ qualitatively from the Abrikosov triangular lattice. In particular, at filling $ν=0.8$, vortices preferentially penetrate weak-pairing regions centered on sites with coordination number $8$, indicating that their spatial organization is strongly influenced by the local geometry. Furthermore, we observe an enhanced upper critical field. At $ν=0.8$, where the enhancement is particularly pronounced, the spatially averaged order parameter exhibits a plateau-like field dependence accompanied by the formation of vortex clusters. These clusters accommodate additional flux in locally weak superconducting regions, providing a microscopic interpretation of the plateau-like behavior. Moreover, the upper critical field increases upon cooling toward zero temperature without a clear sign of saturation.

papers.title_en: Extended Local Infrared Cutoff for the Holographic Density
papers.abstract_en: We propose an extended local infrared cutoff for the holographic density that leads to linear cosmological equations and gives exact analytical solutions. The model allows to remove the residual matter and radiation-like terms of the local construction based on $H$ and $\dot{H}$, resulting in a clear separation between the standard cosmological fluids and the holographic sector. The homogeneous solution generates characteristic modes that give rise to different cosmological behaviors. The extension includes derivatives up to third order, where two of the characteristic modes can modify the pre-recombination expansion and reduce the sound horizon while remaining subdominant at BBN. A slightly phantom mode provides an additional late-time geometrical freedom that can further increase the CMB-compatible value of $H_0$. Optimizations using BAO constraints yield values of $H_0$ in the approximate range $70.5-72.4\ {\rm km\;s^{-1}\;Mpc^{-1}}$.

papers.title_en: Signatures of Lorentz violation in the bright ring for Sgr A* images from radiatively inefficient accretion flows
papers.abstract_en: We have investigated the effects of Lorentz violation (LV) on the bright ring in Sgr A* images illuminated by the 230 GHz thermal synchrotron emission from radiatively inefficient accretion flows around a rotating LV black hole within the low-energy Hořava gravity framework. Our results reveal that the LV parameter reduces the bright ring diameter yet increases its width, luminosity, azimuthal asymmetry and orientation angle. A higher spin parameter strengthens the LV-induced effects on the bright ring properties. Increasing disk thickness reduces the ring diameter and enhances the LV parameter's effects on this diameter. The ring width shows no systematic dependence on the disk thickness. These quantities of the bright ring display similar trends against the black hole spin and the LV parameter for the rotating LV black hole. Using EHT observational data of Sgr A*, we find that, at fixed disk thickness, the parameter-space map illustrates that the bounded range of the LV parameter first broadens and then contracts with the growing black hole spin, and shifts toward smaller LV parameter values. In addition, the LV parameter narrows the bounded range of black hole spin: negative LV parameter values shift this range to a higher spin, while positive values shift it to a lower spin. Finally, we probe effects of the LV parameter on the peak position value and the width of the primary image and the $n=1$ photon ring for the rotating LV black hole. The peak positions and their widths nearly always decrease with the LV parameter. The peak position differences for various LV parameters are more pronounced for a purely Keplerian accretion flow. In addition, the primary image and the $n=1$ photon ring produced by purely radially free-falling flows are broader than their counterparts generated by purely Keplerian flows.

papers.title_en: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
papers.abstract_en: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.

papers.title_en: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
papers.abstract_en: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model in which gauge and Higgs fields are regulated on a finite lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This preserves the familiar continuum description of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes, without requiring a finite-dimensional discretization of chiral fermions. The Standard Model's anomaly cancellation permits a gauge-invariant definition of the chiral fermion determinant. Yukawa interactions are included in the full fermion determinant using a gauge-covariant cutoff that acts on the interaction vertices rather than the fermion propagator. We show that removing this cutoff requires only the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, and construct a consistent complex fermion weight, including in topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At fixed bosonic lattice spacing and finite spacetime volume, the resulting bosonic functional integral is finite and exactly gauge invariant under the stated smoothness conditions. The construction provides a finite-regulator Standard Model formulation retaining the physical structure of continuum chiral fermions. Appendix F.5 establishes reflection positivity for a variant reconstruction at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

papers.title_en: Microscopic study of topological phase transitions: Percolation point of view
papers.abstract_en: We investigate microscopic mechanisms underlying decoherence-induced transitions between topologically ordered states. As a first case study, we analyze the color code using topological entanglement negativity (TEN) and a disorder parameter associated with 1-form symmetry. We interpret these quantities as first- and zeroth-dimensional simplicial homological objects, respectively, and show that the transition can be understood in terms of decoherence percolation. To resolve its local structure, we introduce quasi-local TEN (QLTEN), which visualizes the spatial distribution of local topological properties and the growth of decohered regions. We further introduce explosive percolation (EP), corresponding here to biased decoherence that suppresses the formation of large decohered clusters. As a second case study, we consider the toric code on a triangular lattice under external-field-type decoherence. Numerical results show that QLTEN faithfully captures the emergence of Higgs regions and the survival of logical qubits. Although global TEN, QLTEN clusters, and string operators are strongly correlated in both models, the color code and toric code respond differently to EP patterns. This difference indicates that a universal microscopic description of decoherence-induced topological phase transitions remains challenging even for closely related systems.

papers.title_en: Thermodynamic Phase Transitions in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract_en: Although asymptotically flat black holes generically lack thermodynamic phase transitions, we show that curvature-induced scalarization of electrically charged black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory provides a natural setting for nontrivial thermodynamic behavior, without invoking external confining mechanisms or an extended thermodynamic formalism. Working within the canonical ensemble and employing the Euclidean approach, we identify the coexistence of locally stable scalarized and Reissner-Nordström thermal states, which promotes free-energy crossings to bona fide phase transitions between equilibrium phases. For weak coupling, a second-order phase transition coincides with the second bifurcation point, at which the scalarized branch reconnects with the Reissner-Nordström branch and scalar hair is spontaneously shed. As the coupling strength increases, this transition becomes zeroth order, the scalarized branch shrinks, and a fish-like structure develops in its Helmholtz free energy, rendering locally stable thermal states partially metastable, and yielding up to three phase transitions. In the strong-coupling limit, the scalarized branch reduces to a Schwarzschild-like solution, and the Reissner-Nordström phase ultimately emerges as the sole thermodynamically preferred configuration.

papers.title_en: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

papers.title_en: Chana: A GPU-Accelerated Adaptive-Mesh Code for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics with Multigroup M1 Neutrino Transport
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents Chana, a GPU-accelerated, block-structured adaptive-mesh code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, multigroup M1 neutrino transport, and dynamical spacetime evolution using the Z4c formulation. Each physical module uses independently selected spatial discretizations and ghost-zone widths to balance accuracy and computational cost. Stiff radiation-matter interactions are treated implicitly, with Jacobians calculated analytically from the chain-rules. The code is written in C++20 and it uses MPI and Kokkos 5 for distributed-memory and performance-portable parallelism. The code is validated through a number of GRMHD, radiation transport, and dynamic spacetime tests. For a representative core-collapse supernova configuration with three neutrino species and 12 energy groups per species, the code achieves approximately $1.1 \times 10^6$ cell updates per GPU second on NVIDIA A100 GPUs using four-stage RK4 integration. Weak-scaling efficiency remains above 85\% up to 256 GPUs on Perlmutter.

papers.title_en: Interpreting the $γ$-ray emission from Westerlund 1: hadronic or leptonic?
papers.abstract_en: High-energy $γ$-ray emission has been detected from several star clusters, indicating that these sources are sites of cosmic-ray acceleration. However, it is still unclear whether the $γ$-ray emission is of hadronic or leptonic origin. We present a comprehensive study of the $γ$-ray emission from Westerlund 1, under the assumption that high-energy particles are accelerated at the cluster WTS. We investigate both the hadronic and leptonic scenarios by fitting simultaneously the spectrum and morphology of the $γ$-ray emission. We numerically solve the transport equations for non-thermal protons and electrons for a given $K_\rm{ep}$ and derive their energy and spatial distributions. $γ$ rays are produced either by hadronic pp interactions of protons with the target gas or by inverse Compton scattering of relativistic electrons (both primary and secondary) with the ambient photon fields. We also calculate the synchrotron emission from these electrons. The predicted SEDs are compared with the $γ$-ray measurements by Fermi-LAT and HESS and with the X-ray upper limit derived by eROSITA. For reasonable model parameters, we find that in the case of Bohm diffusion, both the leptonic and hadronic scenarios can account for the observed multi-wavelength spectrum and $γ$-ray morphology. However, in the case of Kraichnan diffusion, better motivated in star clusters, only the hadronic scenario can explain the observations, while the leptonic scenario fails to reproduce the highest-energy $γ$-ray data points. For the leptonic scenario, the magnetic field immediately downstream of the shock can be constrained to be $\lesssim$ a few $μ$G thanks to the eROSITA upper limit. On the other hand, in order to explain the $γ$-ray observations with hadronic emission alone, the gas density inside the bubble should be $\gtrsim 1.2 \, \rm{cm}^{-3}$.

papers.title_en: X-ray Comptonization in an Accreting Kerr Black Hole System with a Tilted Disc and Thermal Corona: A General-Relativistic Monte Carlo Simulation. II. Polarization Signatures
papers.abstract_en: Relativistic precession of the inner accretion flow is widely invoked to explain low-frequency QPOs, and the Relativistic Precession Model (RPM) predicts phase-dependent X-ray polarization. However, IXPE observations challenge simple precession and Comptonization models; for example: SwiftJ1727.8-1613 shows weak or undetected QPO-phase polarization modulation, while IGRJ17091-3624 shows a hard-state polarization degree (DOP) of ~9%, versus ~4% in other hard-state black hole binaries. In Paper I, we presented a general-relativistic Monte Carlo (GRMC) model of X-ray reprocessing in a misaligned, warped two-zone disc around a Kerr black hole with a hot, optically thin corona. We computed energy spectra, photon path-length and arrival-time distributions, and X-ray lags. Here, we extend the model to track photon polarization using Walker-Penrose parallel transport and polarized Compton and disc scattering. We calculate the energy-resolved degree and angle of polarization and their precession-phase modulation versus coronal optical depth, outer-disc albedo, photon-injection radius, and observer inclination. We find that gravitational light bending raises the mean DOP and enhances modulation, whereas coronal scattering and reflection from the misaligned outer disc lower the DOP and suppress modulation. The steady outer-disc polarization further dilutes the inner-flow signal. Their competition can produce weak, nearly unmodulated polarization or a high, strongly modulated signal. Strong scattering and reflection can explain SwiftJ1727.8-1613's weak modulation, while strong light bending and weak secondary scattering can explain IGRJ17091-3624's high DOP. Our results provide a framework for interpreting unusual X-ray polarization and testable predictions for constraining black hole parameters, coronal properties, and disc-warp geometry with IXPE, XPoSat, and eXTP.

papers.title_en: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract_en: Despite the growing application of large language models (LLMs) to theoretical physics, there has been little academic exploration of how domain-specific physics reasoning ability develops during training. To investigate this, we perform the first academic comparison of reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for LLMs on verifiable problem-solving tasks in theoretical physics. Because the open-source verifiable training data required to develop such capabilities is scarce, we built a robust data generation pipeline that can both create synthetic problems and make existing human-authored problems suitable for model training. Selecting quantum field theory (QFT) as our primary domain, we generated over 2,500 synthetic problems alongside a curated collection of human-adapted problems sourced from arXiv and standard pedagogical resources. We conduct both reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) experiments, benchmarking performance gains as well as generalization to other physics domains. Although both methods improve over the base model on every dataset, SFT gains are concentrated on in-distribution synthetic tasks, while RL generalizes better, outperforming SFT on the human-adapted datasets and TPBench. We perform an extensive analysis of model chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning before and after fine-tuning to understand how reasoning errors evolve during RL and SFT. Finally, we publicly release our data pipeline, verifiable QFT training data, and ~200M tokens of QFT reasoning traces.
papers.journal_ref: Nathaniel S Woodward et al 2026 Mach. Learn.: Sci. Technol. 7 055029

papers.title_en: Scale Anomaly in Supersymmetric Quantum Electrodynamics: Ward Identities, Supersymmetry Breaking, and Decoupling
papers.abstract_en: We study the breaking of the scale symmetry both within classical and quantum frameworks in the supersymmetric quantum electrodynamics (SQED) by applying a four-dimensional regularization that preserves supersymmetry. At the classical level, scale symmetry is shown to be broken by mass terms. At the quantum level, it is demonstrated to be broken by a term proportional to the SQED beta function in the massless limit. It is also shown how this anomaly manifests itself in the low- and high-energy limits and how the Appelquist-Carazzone theorem reproduces the usual quantum electrodynamics result in the limit of heavy selectrons.

papers.title_en: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse
papers.abstract_en: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes undergo gravothermal evolution whose late-time behaviour is central to predictions for dense substructure and black-hole seed formation. We revisit the calibration of this evolution using a new spherical Direct Simulation Monte Carlo code, SphDSMC, which follows spherically symmetric SIDM systems without force softening and to substantially higher central densities than standard N-body simulations. We compare SphDSMC calculations with conventional N-body simulations and with one-dimensional gravothermal fluid models. We show that N-body results converge to SphDSMC only for softening lengths significantly smaller than those normally adopted for collisionless simulations, and that allowing multiple scatterings per particle per time step does not introduce significant errors when implemented appropriately. Calibrating the gravothermal fluid equations against SphDSMC, we find that the commonly used harmonic interpolation between the long- and short-mean-free-path conductivities is inaccurate. A gentler transition, however, yields excellent agreement for NFW haloes over a range of concentrations and truncation radii, with a single long-mean-free-path conductivity parameter. The revised calibration gives a long-mean-free-path collapse time that is somewhat shorter than previous estimates, but we show that collapse slows dramatically once the core becomes optically thick. We provide fitting functions for the late-time evolution and argue that black-hole seed formation by SIDM gravothermal collapse has generally been underestimated in duration, making it unlikely to explain the massive high-redshift black holes inferred from JWST observations without additional physics.

papers.title_en: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
papers.abstract_en: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.

papers.title_en: Black Holes, Moduli Stabilisation and the Swampland
papers.abstract_en: In theories with moduli, extremal black holes behave such that for generic initial conditions, the distance traveled by the scalars from infinity to the horizon can grow with the size of the black hole. This, in turn, implies that larger black holes can probe more of the UV ingredients of the theory, in contrast with (naive) EFT expectations. We relate this discrepancy to the lack of cosmological moduli stabilisation. Indeed, for would-be scale-separated string vacua with parametrically heavy stabilised scalars -- dubbed \emph{rigid} compactifications -- one recovers the EFT intuition where only small black holes probe the UV. We make this explicit in a toy model and then turn to top-down models and construct near-horizon solutions in IIA scale-separated compactifications with stabilised moduli. In these top-down models we still observe large field variations for large black holes which can be traced back to the absence of parametrically heavy moduli. We are led to speculate that needing UV physics to allow for non-local effects near the horizon of large black holes is at odds with having a rigid compactification, hinting to the possibility that such compactifications are in the Swampland.

papers.title_en: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
papers.abstract_en: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the $Λ$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $η(z)\equiv D_{\rm L}/[{(1+z)}^2D_{\rm A}]=α{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon\neq0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $Λ$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $Λ$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $Ω_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $η(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $η(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z<0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $α\simeq0.942\pm0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also discuss photon-loss and varying-$G$ interpretations: ordinary positive opacity cannot explain the negative central tilts $\varepsilon$ found for a $Λ$CDM background, while local gravity tests strongly constrain the illustrative unscreened varying-$G$ scenario.

papers.title_en: Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy of Ce and U Oxides
papers.abstract_en: The soft x-ray Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy (RIPES) of the M5 transition in cerium oxide and the N5 transition in uranium dioxide and supporting instrumentation is discussed.
